key_insight: Disk-like droplets with high circularity and expansion favor dense Fe-based amorphous coatings, while greater porosity reduces long-term corrosion resistance and higher humidity lowers friction and wear.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce denser coatings on Q235 steel, with service humidity influencing wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, lamellar structure, and coating porosity.
Test long-term corrosion and sliding wear under different humidity conditions using Si3N4 balls.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports poorer long-term corrosion resistance with greater porosity and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases, without numerical results.
watch_item: Humidity-dependent wear findings involve Si3N4 counterfaces and should not be assumed to apply to other contact materials.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
